A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same research work and contain readable main text, figures, tables, equations and supplementary Sections A–E. Corresponding methods, experiments and appendix content can be reliably matched.

before.justification: V1 reports original camera-visibility analyses, pose-estimation experiments on Ego4View-Syn and Ego4View-RW, component ablations and supplementary per-action results.

after.justification: V2 retains these original empirical results and additionally reports baseline heatmap errors in Table 5.

M1.justification: Sections 4.1–4.5 retain the same attention-based refinement, heatmap/RGB embeddings, uncertainty masking, loss and 3D lifting components. V2 explicitly clarifies interaction across all views and repetition of refinement for each view; both operations were already described in v1.

E1.justification: Training and evaluation still use Ego4View-Syn and Ego4View-RW with the same tasks, populations and camera configurations. SimpleEgo is added only to the dataset catalogue in Table 1, not used in experiments. The new hair-obstruction limitation is not an evaluated scenario.

E2.justification: Table 5 adds unrefined EgoPoseFormer, labelled 'Baseline [54]', to the ablation comparison. Although already evaluated in Table 3, it was absent from v1's Table 5. The main benchmark comparisons otherwise retain EgoTAP and EgoPoseFormer.

E3.justification: The splits, input resolutions, training stages and budgets, batch sizes, learning-rate schedule, camera configurations and evaluation metrics remain unchanged. V2 explicitly states that baselines are retrained on the proposed datasets, but does not establish a revised protocol or new training runs.

E4.justification: The added unrefined baseline row in Table 5 provides a reference for assessing heatmap refinement and component ablations. Existing ablation variants, visibility analyses, qualitative examples and supplementary per-action analyses remain unchanged.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, significance tests or experimental error bars. The retained heatmap-uncertainty mechanism is a model component, not statistical uncertainty reporting.

E6.justification: Table 5 newly reports baseline front/back heatmap MSEs of 2.30/3.36 in units of 10^-4/pixel. Its baseline MPJPE/PA-MPJPE values, 20.20/17.63 mm, repeat existing Table 3 results. Existing benchmark and ablation scores, qualitative findings and supplementary per-action values are unchanged.

T1.justification: Equations 1–11 and their mathematical definitions remain equivalent. The motivation based on complementary front/rear observations is retained, and neither version adds formal propositions, proofs or derivations.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction's contribution list and conclusion retain the same central claims: investigating rear cameras for full-body tracking, proposing transformer-based heatmap refinement, introducing two Ego4View datasets and achieving over 10% improvement on Ego4View-RW.

C2.justification: V2 adds a substantive limitation concerning frizzy or voluminous hair obstructing camera views. It also specifies an example of the existing extreme-self-occlusion failure and proposes physics-based motion priors as future work, replacing v1's generic suggestion to improve physical plausibility.

D1.justification: Section 3 newly identifies multi-view video and EasyMocap as the source of real-world SMPL parameters, and Section 5.2 explicitly documents baseline retraining. The abstract changes from promising resource release to stating that code, models and datasets are available. Existing hyperparameters and supplementary architecture, hardware and speed details remain.

R1.justification: V2 adds citations to EasyMocap, SimpleEgo and EventEgo3D++, and adds SimpleEgo to Table 1. It removes Section 3's claim that Ego4View-RW is the first body-facing RGB dataset offering hand and SMPL parameters, modestly narrowing dataset novelty positioning.

P1.justification: V2 makes local grammatical corrections, clarifies method descriptions, tightens the conclusion, shortens several headings and adds an acknowledgment. The overall narrative, section order and supplementary Sections A–E remain intact.

P2.justification: Tables 1 and 5 gain rows, Tables 3 and 4 are repositioned, and supplementary Table I becomes Table 6 without changing its results. Captions receive limited clarification, including the meaning of visibility percentages in Table 2. The figures retain their substantive visual content.

improvement.justification: V2 improves transparency through annotation provenance and explicit retraining information, strengthens Table 5 with baseline heatmap errors, and provides a more concrete account of practical limitations. Adding SimpleEgo and withdrawing the dataset-priority claim also improves research positioning. These are useful, limited gains; the method, main experimental results and supplementary evidence remain essentially unchanged.
